Description
Figs. 3a and 3b show the motor drive with its cover 35 removed.

The drive with terminal section is dust tight
and water proof, the model for plug connection is dust tight.
The heating resistors 67.prevent condensation. They must always be in circuit.
The terminal section of units likely to be exposed to temperatures
below-25oC (down to -50oC) is provided with two heating
resistors ,which must be switched on during the cold season but may be switched
off when it gets warmer.
The gearing is pre lubricated. The
gearing compartment is connected with the control and terminal compartment by
vents and must never be filled with grease.

Laying the pipes and cables Laying the SF6 
pipes

The gas-filled compartments are connected with each other with 
the control unit and with the gas-monitoring panel as shown in the special pipe 
diagrams and layout plans furnished for each installation. 
Use the pipe fittings etc. supplied with the switchgear as separate items.

Some of the pipe sections are pre-assembled at the factory but 
long pipe connections have to be made at the site

Care should be taken to avoid formation of oxides (sealing) caused
by heat during brazing. For this purpose pass a protective gas through the pipe 
while brazing.

Don't use any flux Use a solder containing phosphorus (e.g.L-Ag 15 
P DIN 8513 and ISO 3677)

Laying the control and signaling cables

The control and signaling cables should be laid and connected up 
the accordance with the special diagrams supplied for the switchgear. The 
cable ducts. clip fittings and clips etc. are supplied as separate items.
Charging the filters

The filters must not be exposed to a humid atmosphere. Their 
filling must therefore not be in contact with the air for more than 15 
minutes. The filter material is supplied in small bags of 175g and in large 
bags of 260g in sealed tins.

When the tins are properly sealed. a vacuum forms which is 
recognizable by a clearly audible hissing sound as the tins are opened. If a tin 
is no longer properly sealed. the vacuum collapses and the filter material will 
absorb moisture. Filter material from improperly
sealed tins should therefore not be employed because the filter capacity will no longer be adequate for the 
maintenance interval specified.

When installation has been completed and 
immediately prior to evacuating the breaker and filling in the SF6. position 
the filter bags at the points indicated in the basic circuit diagram and the 
master drawing. These points are also marked by adhesive labels ... filter
Proceed as follows:

Unscrew the covers concerned. place the page 
in the filter and immediately refit the cover (fig. 3/24 and fig. 3/25)

The quantity of filter material stated in the drawings normally
suffices for an operating period of 10 years. If the voltage transformer is 
directly mounted on a busbar chamber (measuring bay. ct. fig. 2/8), a SF6 filter 
coupling is to be used instead of the coupling shown in fig. 3/26. This 
additionally contains a filter to prevent contamination of the relatively large 
busbar chamber in case of a fault in the voltage transformer. The connection is 
to be made in the same way as described above.

Filling in SF6 and checking the
settings of the contact-making manometers

The SF6 used for insulating and arc-quenching purposes can be 
purposes in from a service unit which is fully equipped for this purpose.If 
no service unit is available the sf6 can be taken from gas cylinders. (SF6 
filling device W 294 : see operating instructions for the circuit-breaker) A 
vacuum pump must then be made available so that the gas-filled sections can 
first 
be evacuated.

Contact-making manometers have adjustable pointers 
fitted with 
electrical contacts. When the pressure drops to the preset value, the contacts 
close and initiate a signal
Important

The SF6 gas should not be blown into covers with filter (e.g. fig. 3/25) as this 
is likely 
to damage the filter bag.

The motor drives worm wheel
27.va worm31, the rotary motion being transmitted to drive shaft 80.through spur
gears 25,99,95 and 93.(fig.4a). the stop 85.releases plunger 65, the cup springs
69 are discharged and lever 55.turns auxiliary switch 53.into the half-way
position .At the end of the rotary motion the stop 91.runs up against the
left-hand plunger 51.which is damped by cup spring. and the auxiliary switch is
moved into its end position by lever 55.

The shaft extension of the motor
has a hexagon shank 39.for manual operation. This shank becomes accessible by
removing cover 45.as a result of which limit switch 47.interrupts the motor
circuit.

The compression glands 5.1 for entering the control and auxiliary cables in the 
motor drive with terminal section are located in the adapter section 5.this can 
be fitted in either of two positions to permit the supply to be connected on the 
control-section side or the gear-section side.

The control and auxiliary
cables are connected to the terminal blocks5. after removal of cowl 3.
For the motor drive with plug connection the control and auxiliary cables are
wired to plugs.

sections.text: Installation

The drive is shipped
together with the isolator/earthing switch, ready for

The drive must not be stored
outdoors for more than three 
months without the anti-condensation heater being switched on.

If this period 
has been exceeded. the drive must be inspected before being installed. The 
supplier cannot be held responsible for any damage caused by corrosion.

The 
drive, which is specially equipped for use with the switch, must be secured in 
its final mounting position so that the openings of the venting stubs and 
compression glands are facing downwards.Drill fixing holes into the 
supporting plate or other support and firmly bolt on the drive using the fixing 
bolts (complete with flat washers and spring washers) supplied

Tighten the 
bolts uniformly in diagonal sequence.

Enter the control and auxiliary cables 
in the motor drive with terminal section through the compression glands and 
connect them to the terminal blocks in accordance with the table supplied. when 
the connections have been made check to see that the sealing faces of the 
adapter section and the gasket 3.1 of cowl 3. are clean.

Replace the cowl and 
tighten the screws uniformly. (Apply a small amount of talcum to gasket 3.1 to 
prevent an adhesive effect) If the motor drive is equipped for plug 
connection, fit the plug with the control and auxiliary cables

The installation of the cowl : Set up the cowl in the correct 
position (Fig. 3a,3b) on the stay-bolts which are guiding the cowl. Before press 
the gasket on the housing, guide the centering-pins in the belonging center 
bore. Now screw on the grip nut symmetrical.

Do not cant the cowl when it setting up, it is possible to 
damage the housing respectively the gasket is out of duty.

When work on the 
motor drive has been completed and immediately prior to putting it into 
operation remove the adhesive tape from the six vents and the plastic plugs from 
the venting stubs.

Before carring out any other work on the drive, i.e. work 
where the risk of foreign matter entering cannot be ruled out, seal the 
particular apertures with adhesive tape.

Remember to remove the adhesive tape, so that the gear compartment is adequately 
vented.

sections.text: Operation

The drive can also be actuated by hand in case 
the supply should fail. Use a hand-crank with 13 mm 
width across flats and a (slipper) clutch (Fig.5), or a hand drill (Fig.6). 
These tools are only supplied to special order.

To actuate the drive by hand, remove the two wing screws 43. 
(Fig.4a) and withdraw cover 45. Following this. place the hand-crank or the hand 
drill on hexagon shank 39. Operate the drive by turning the hand-crank or hand 
drill, paying due attention to the symbols "O" for off and "l" for On on the 
drive cowl.

Slipping of the (slipper) clutch indicates either that friction 
in the mechanism is excessive or that the particular position has been 
reached.

Maintenance, Spare parts

The drive requires no maintenance. The 
gearing is pre-lubricated at the factory.

It is advisable to lift off cowl 35. (Fig. 3) after six years to check the 
control section

Furthermore, the seal 35.5 and the sealing ring 45.5 and 59.1 (Fig. 4) should 
be checked and replaced if necessary.

The following data should be given when ordering spare parts:
 1. Order No. of the Operating Instructions;
 2. Description and part No. to table below or from Fig. 4
 3. Serial No. of the isolator / earthing switch

Operation
The drive can also be actuated by hand in case 
the supply should fail. Use a hand-crank with 13 mm 
width across flats and a (slipper) clutch (Fig.5), or a hand drill (Fig.6). 
These tools are only supplied to special order.
To actuate the drive by hand, remove the two wing screws 43. 
(Fig.4a) and withdraw cover 45. Following this. place the hand-crank or the hand 
drill on hexagon shank 39. Operate the drive by turning the hand-crank or hand 
drill, paying due attention to the symbols "O" for off and "l" for On on the 
drive cowl.
Slipping of the (slipper) clutch indicates either that friction 
in the mechanism is excessive or that the particular position has been 
reached.
